questions.q: What is a Snowflake resource monitor?
options: A Power BI feature unrelated to Snowflake warehouses
A dashboard that requires a person to manually check credit usage every day
A credit-quota object attached to one or more warehouses (or the account) that automatically triggers actions when consumption crosses defined thresholds
A tool that only works after credits have already been overspent
questions.explain: A resource monitor enforces itself once created and attached — no human has to keep checking a dashboard for it to take action.

questions.q: In a CREATE RESOURCE MONITOR statement, what does the TRIGGERS clause with ON 100 PERCENT DO SUSPEND do?
options: Sends only a notification email with no effect on running queries
Immediately cancels every currently running query the instant 100% is reached
Permanently deletes the warehouse
Blocks new queries from starting once 100% of the credit quota is used, but lets already-running queries finish
questions.explain: SUSPEND is the graceful stop — it blocks new queries but allows in-flight queries to complete, unlike SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE.

questions.q: How does SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE differ from SUSPEND?
options: SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE only sends a notification, like NOTIFY
SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE only affects storage cost, not compute
SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE blocks new queries AND cancels all currently running queries right away, while SUSPEND lets running queries finish
They are identical in every way
questions.explain: SUSPEND_IMMEDIATE is the hard stop — a true circuit breaker that cancels in-flight work, unlike the graceful SUSPEND.

questions.q: How do you attach a resource monitor to a specific warehouse?
options: ALTER WAREHOUSE <warehouse_name> SET RESOURCE_MONITOR = <monitor_name>;
CREATE RESOURCE MONITOR automatically attaches itself to every warehouse
Resource monitors cannot be attached to individual warehouses, only the account
DROP WAREHOUSE <warehouse_name> SET RESOURCE_MONITOR = <monitor_name>;
questions.explain: Creating a resource monitor does nothing until it's attached via ALTER WAREHOUSE ... SET RESOURCE_MONITOR (or ALTER ACCOUNT for account-wide default).

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a statement timeout in addition to a resource monitor?
options: Statement timeouts replace the need for resource monitors entirely
They serve identical purposes and using both is redundant
Statement timeouts control storage cost, which resource monitors cannot
A resource monitor caps total spend over a period, but won't catch one runaway query burning credits for hours before the period quota is reached
questions.explain: A resource monitor and a statement timeout catch different failure modes — a period-level budget vs. a per-query runtime cap — and work well together, not as substitutes.
